facts.text: Mullan, Idaho, takes its name from West Point graduate John Mullan, who mapped the historic Mullan Road linking Montana to Washington.
Gold struck at the Gold Hunter Mine in 1884 sparked Mullan’s birth, turning the area into a bustling lead‑silver mining hub.
The Northern Pacific Railway arrived in 1889, cementing Mullan’s role as a key rail stop in the Silver Valley.
The Mullan Museum, founded in 1984, sits in the historic IOOF building on Earle Street, preserving the town’s mining legacy.
Inside the museum, a photo collection showcases miners battling the 1957 Morning Mill Fire and the bustling 1955 Northern Pacific Depot.
Nestled in a sheltered canyon of the Coeur d'Alene Mountains, Mullan sits at 3,278 feet above sea level.
